 LIVE  Updated  30s ago Scott Murray Wed 28 Oct 2026 16.29 EDT First published on Wed 28 Oct 2026 14.30 EDT Share Key events 2h ago The teams 
 2h ago Preamble 
 We’re under way at Anfield!
 Photograph: Paul Currie/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen We’re under way at Anfield!
 Photograph: Paul Currie/Shutterstock Scott Murray Wed 28 Oct 2026 16.29 EDT First published on Wed 28 Oct 2026 14.30 EDT Share Key events 2h ago The teams 
 2h ago Preamble 
 29s ago 16.29 EDT 28 min: Ngumoha takes on Acheampong down the left and wins Liverpool another corner. Tsimikas’s delivery isn’t great, but Nyoni recovers the clearance 40 yards from goal … only to butcher the chance to release Gakpo down the middle. Penders still hasn’t been put to work.
 Share 3m ago 16.27 EDT 26 min: The goals are flying in elsewhere. Malick Fofana has put Sunderland 3-0 up at home to Brentford, while Eddie Nketiah has given Crystal Palace a 37th-minute lead at Fulham.
 Share 4m ago 16.25 EDT 24 min: Rogers and Araujo tangle as the former drives into the Liverpool box from the left. Rogers goes over and demands a penalty; the referee waves play on. No VAR, so there’s no second chance for Chelsea … and there was some contact. As ever with refereeing decisions these days, nobody knows anything. You’ve seen them given.
 Share 5m ago 16.24 EDT 23 min: Ngumoha glides down the left and feeds Tsimikas on the overlap. Tsimikas’s low cross is easily intercepted and cleared, much to the Kop’s displeasure. Lovely initial surge by Ngumoha, though.
 Share 7m ago 16.23 EDT 22 min: From the resulting free kick, Caicedo scuffs a poor shot wide left. That’s the first effort from either side, and it wasn’t very good. Onwards and upwards.
 Share 8m ago 16.22 EDT 21 min: McConnell goes haring after his own heavy touch, then swats the ball away from Rogers with his hand. He goes into the book. He can have no complaints.
 Share Updated at  16.22 EDT 9m ago 16.20 EDT 20 min: Caicedo goes over looking for a foul. He doesn’t get it, and tells it as he sees it to the referee, who thinks about booking him but stops at a lecture. Caicedo might not have much more rope. The home fans aren’t happy, but then neither is Henderson.
 Share 11m ago 16.18 EDT 18 min: Tsimikas advances down the left and crosses low. McConnell hovers, so Caicedo is forced to nip in and blooter behind for the first corner of the evening. Gakpo takes, but the whistle goes for a shove by Tsimikas on Gusto.
 Share 13m ago 16.17 EDT 16 min: McConnell tries to power in from the left but is upended. No foul, and it’s fair to say the Kop haven’t warmed to the referee so far.
 Share 14m ago 16.15 EDT 14 min: Mateo Kovacic has levelled things up for Manchester City against Brighton. Meanwhile it’s a quickfire double for Sunderland against Brentford: Chemsdine Talbi and Tymur Tutierov with two goals in three minutes. It’s 2-0 to the hosts at the Stadium of Light.
 View image in fullscreen Mateo Kovacic scores a beauty to level things up at the Etihad. Photograph: Dave Thompson/AP Share Updated at  16.21 EDT 16m ago 16.13 EDT 12 min: Gravenberch clips Caicedo just to the right of the Liverpool D. Chelsea want a free kick, but the referee waves play on. Henderson can’t keep the move going. Liverpool get away with one there. Not a banner 60 seconds for the ref, you’d have to say.
 Share 18m ago 16.12 EDT 11 min: Araujo intercepts 40 yards out, and feeds Koumas ahead of him. Koumas tries to release Gakpo down the middle. The pass doesn’t come off. Lacroix tries to run the ball back upfield, but is blocked by Koumas. It’s a foul; it’s a very harsh booking. But into the book he goes, and it’ll be a long evening for a player with a whole-hearted, no-nonsense pressing style.
 Share 20m ago 16.10 EDT 9 min: Acheampong takes his time over a throw; then Lacroix gets methodical over a goal kick. The 2014 version of Jose Mourinho would surely approve.
 Share 22m ago 16.07 EDT 7 min: Tsimikas delivers, but not particularly accurately. Chelsea clear their lines without too much fuss.
 Share 23m ago 16.07 EDT 6 min: Ngumoha probes down the left and is fairly crudely brought down by Neto, who hangs out a leg to put a stop to the winger’s gallop. A free kick just to the side of the penalty box, which is now full of players of both stripe.
 Share 24m ago 16.06 EDT 5 min: Some goals elsewhere to report. Amine Adli has given Bournemouth a seventh-minute lead against Aston Villa, while Malick Yalcouye has bundled Brighton & Hove Albion ahead on the half-hour at Manchester City.
 View image in fullscreen Malick Yalcouye scores for Brighton! Photograph: Matt West/Shutterstock Share Updated at  16.10 EDT 25m ago 16.04 EDT 4 min: Ngumoha had a great game on the right against Villarreal last week. He’s started out on the left tonight, though. Otherwise, not so much to report in these early exchanges.
 View image in fullscreen Rio Ngumoha runs clear of Josh Acheampong. Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock Share Updated at  16.12 EDT 27m ago 16.02 EDT 2 min: “Do you think Henderson’s relishing his return?” wonder-quips Kevin Dwyer. “Sorry, it’s our favourite condiment.” He was chewing gum quite ferociously as he emerged from the tunnel. He’ll have been thinking about this evening quite a bit, I’ll be bound.
 Share 29m ago 16.00 EDT Basque pals Andoni and Xabi embrace warmly … but so much for friendship, because Chelsea turn Liverpool around, so the home side are kicking towards the Kop in this first half. They’re not huge fans of that. They kick off.
 Share 31m ago 15.59 EDT The teams are out! Liverpool in red, Chelsea in blue. These lads always look good when they play each other. We’ll be off in a couple of minutes!
 The Joy of Six: great Chelsea v Liverpool moments and matches | Scott Murray Read more Share 39m ago 15.51 EDT Xabi Alonso – a European champion with Liverpool but having suffered two defeats out of two as a visiting manager with Bayer Leverkusen and Real Madrid – speaks to Sky Sports. “The cups are important for us this year … we have a good challenge here coming to Anfield … it’s make or break … we want to make it happen today … we know we need a great performance … we have taken [this competition] from the beginning seriously … our players have played a few times already here … hopefully they will show it today.”
 Share 43m ago 15.46 EDT Pre-match postbag. “I’m loving the balance of experience and youth in the Liverpool starting XI. Jürgen had Klopp’s kids. Arne could have rolled out Slot’s Snappers more often. Today we’ve got Iraola’s Imps!” – Peter Oh
 “Looking at the Liverpool line-up, I can only think that Iraola has decided not to risk the prospect of drawing the mighty Fleetwood Town in the next round” – Vanessa Edwards
 “For the sake of the integrity of the Carabao Cup I think we are all Brighton fans tonight. If City stay in the competition and then lose their appeal (almost inevitable) then how on earth does that get resolved?” – Rick Harris
 “Anfield is nine miles from where I currently slouch and I can feel the anticipation from here. Something might just be afoot. Hope? Hendo also returns. But am glad he has scored his one cracker for the season already” – Ian Copestake (and readers who enjoy making speculative investments may be interested to note that, now Ian’s said that, you can get 28s on Henderson scoring the first goal tonight)
 Share 1h ago 15.14 EDT Andoni Iraola speaks to Sky Sports. “We need fresh legs … a lot of players are waiting for this competition to have their starts, their minutes … they are pushing hard … so I have trust that they can perform well … the bench is always important … we have good options … according to how the game goes, we will decide one way or another … we need to keep winning games … we need to keep going … it does not stop … the level of our opposition is very high … everyone has to play their part … I hope today they do … Chelsea have a very strong starting XI … we have to respect them … we have to be at our very best if we want to beat them … we always practice [penalties] … I don’t know if it is better or worse, I think Fleetwood didn’t practice and they were incredible! … but we always do it!”
 Share 1h ago 15.09 EDT A reminder that the draw for the quarter-finals will take place tonight. The tombola is scheduled to begin spinning at around 10.20pm UK time, so we can probably add 10-20 minutes to that, The Man is notorious for dragging his feet at these things. There are already two balls in the spinner: Bradford City and Fleetwood Town, the latter having done a proper number on the reigning champions of England last night.
 Max Dowman’s Fleetwood fracas leaves him, Arsenal and Arteta red-faced Read more Football Daily | Fleetwood go their own way to down Arsenal and live Carabao Cup dream Read more Share 2h ago 14.55 EDT Chelsea make four changes after their 0-2 home reverse to Tottenham Hotspur. Danny Welbeck, Roméo Lavia, Malo Gusto and Wesley Fofana come in for Levi Colwill and Geovany Quenda, who are benched, the injured Jorrel Hato, and the suspended Cole Palmer.
 Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham: Premier League – as it happened Read more Share 2h ago 14.53 EDT Liverpool make seven changes to their starting XI following the 2-0 win at the weekend over Brighton. Giorgi Mamardashvili, Joe Gomez, Kostas Tsimikas, Trey Nyoni, James McConnell, Lewis Koumas and Rio Ngumoha are in; Alisson, Jérémy Jacquet, Florian Wirtz, Alexis Mac Allister, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak drop to the bench, while Milos Kerkez misses out altogether.
 Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end Read more Share 2h ago 14.46 EDT The teams
 Liverpool: Mamardashvili, Gomez, van Dijk, Araujo, Tsimikas, Gravenberch, Nyoni, Ngumoha, McConnell, Gakpo, Koumas.
 Subs: Alisson, Endo, Jacquet, Wirtz, Isak, Mac Allister, Chiesa, Barcola, Chambers. 
 Chelsea: Penders, Gusto, Lacroix, Fofana, Acheampong, Henderson, Caicedo, Lavia, Pedro Neto, Welbeck, Rogers.
 Subs: Sharman-Lowe, Colwill, Subuloye, Palestra, Barco, Nicoll-Jazuli, Estevao, Quenda, Emegha. 
 Referee: Darren England.
VAR: No VAR! 
 Share Updated at  15.10 EDT 2h ago 14.30 EDT Preamble
 Welcome to a re-run of this … 
 Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties to win Carabao Cup final – as it happened Read more … and this …
 Chelsea 0-1 Liverpool (aet): Carabao Cup final, extra time – as it happened Read more … the narrative of which can only be successfully told and subsequently analysed through the prism of tonight’s team selections. And let’s face it, you’ll be doing well to predict those accurately. News when we have it, and we’ll take it from there. Kick-off is at 8pm GMT. It’s on!
